blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: The search for computationally efficient alternatives to the Transformer has yielded numerous architectures in recent years; however, most exhibit severe weaknesses in associative recall-such as key-value (KV) retrieval-and length extrapolation, where even standard Transformers struggle. This paper introduces LimeTree, a linear-complexity architecture in both memory and compute for sequence modeling. By integrating synthetic KV retrieval tasks directly into standard language modeling training, LimeTree achieves strong perplexity alongside reliable recall. Two variants were evaluated on WikiText-103 and PG-19 under strict compute constraints. On WikiText-103, LimeTree reaches a token-level perplexity of 19 in just 6 hours on four Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs, while maintaining 100\% KV retrieval accuracy even when extrapolating from a training context length of 512 to an evaluation length of 16,384. On PG-19, the model achieves a token-level perplexity of 13 in 35 hours on a single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU with minimal hyperparameter tuning. These results position LimeTree as a competitive linear-complexity alternative to Transformers, combining superior perplexity and training throughput with robust in-context retrieval and length extrapolation.
blocks.zh: 近年来,在寻找计算效率高的变形器替代物的过程中,产生了许多架构;然而,大多数架构在诸如键值(KV)检索法和长度推算法等关联性召回法中表现出严重弱点,甚至标准变形器在其中挣扎. 本文引入了LimeTree,一种线性复合结构,既包含内存,也包含序列模型的计算. 通过将合成的KV检索任务直接纳入标准语言建模训练,LimeTree在可靠召回的同时实现了强烈的迷惑性. 在严格计算限制下,WikiText-103和PG-19上评价了两种变体. 在WikiText-103上,LimeTree在4台Quadro RTX 8000 GPU上仅6小时就达到了19个符号级的迷惑度,同时保持100QQ KV检索精度,即使从训练背景长度512到评价长度16,384的推断. 在PG-19上,该型号在单张RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU上以最小的超参数调制,在35小时内实现13个符号级的复杂度. 这些结果将LimeTree定位为替代变形器的竞争性线性复合性,结合了优异的复杂性和培训的吞吐量与强力的内文本检索和长度推算.

blocks.en: Highlights
blocks.zh: 要点

blocks.en: • Predictable, Linear Infrastructure Costs: Standard AI models (Transformers) become exponentially more expensive as inputs get longer, driving up cloud compute and hardware bills. LimeTree’s memory and compute scale strictly linearly, enabling lightweight models that process massive contexts at a fraction of standard deployment and inference costs. • Train Cheaply on Short Data, Deploy on Massive Contexts: Models typically require exorbitant budgets to train on long documents. LimeTree can be trained affordably on short sequences (4,096 tokens) and immediately process 128× longer inputs (over 524,000 tokens—roughly 1,000 pages of text) out of the box with negligible loss in accuracy. • Proven Foundation with High Upside: Even as an unoptimized first-generation architecture, LimeTree matches the mid-tier performance of mature, heavily engineered industry baselines—offering an immediate, scalable foundation for proprietary long-context LLMs with substantial headroom for performance gains.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Since its introduction, the Transformer architecture as presented in Vaswani et al. (2017) has become the foundational backbone of modern artificial intelligence, evolving from early sequence-to-sequence machine translation models into general-purpose foundation models across natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal domains. More recently, the capabilities of these models have been substantially expanded by augmenting next-token prediction with test-time compute Snell et al. (2024) , explicit reasoning chains Wei et al. (2022) , and tree-search algorithms such as Monte Carlo Tree Search Kocsis and Szepesvári (2006) ; Silver et al. (2016) ; Yao et al. (2023) ; Hao et al. (2023) . By integrating these search mechanisms, language models have transitioned from passive text generators into autonomous agents capable of complex planning, iterative self-correction, and multi-step problem solving. However, this shift toward deep reasoning and expansive search trees drastically
increases the number of generated tokens and active context requirements,
amplifying the underlying computational bottlenecks of the standard
self-attention mechanism ( Vaswani et al., 2017 ) . Chain-of-thought
prompting ( Wei et al., 2022 ) , tree-structured search ( Yao et al., 2023 ) ,
scaling of test-time compute ( Snell et al., 2024 ) , and reinforcement-learned
reasoning models ( OpenAI, 2024 ; DeepSeek-AI, 2025 ) all trade longer
generations for accuracy.

To mitigate these scaling costs, extensive research has focused on developing
sub-quadratic alternatives to attention. Early linear-attention variants, such as
Linformer ( Wang et al., 2020 ) and Performer ( Choromanski et al., 2021 ) ,
as well as pure recurrent formulations like Receptance Weighted Key Value
architectures ( Peng and others, 2023 ) , demonstrated theoretical efficiency gains but
have seen limited adoption in publicly documented frontier systems, with
performance degradation relative to softmax attention reported in recall-sensitive
settings ( Katharopoulos et al., 2020 ; Arora and others, 2024 ) . Similarly, early
structured state-space models (SSMs) like S4 ( Gu et al., 2022 ) ,
H3 ( Fu et al., 2023 ) , and Hyena ( Poli and others, 2023 ) largely remain confined
to specialized research settings or domain-specific tasks. In contrast, selective
state-space models—most notably Mamba ( Gu and Dao, 2024 ) and
Mamba-2 ( Dao and Gu, 2024 ) —alongside gated linear RNNs such as
Griffin ( De and others, 2024 ) , xLSTM ( Beck and others, 2024 ) , and
RetNet ( Sun and others, 2023 ) , have achieved meaningful practical traction.
Even among these stronger contenders, pure sub-quadratic architectures exhibit
well-documented weaknesses in copying and in-context recall ( Jelassi et al., 2024 ; Arora and others, 2024 ; Waleffe and others, 2024 ) ; consequently,
among openly documented production-scale systems, hybrid architectures-such as

MiniMax-01 ( MiniMax, 2025 ) , and Nemotron-H ( NVIDIA, 2025 ) —predominate,

recall.

blocks.en: While Transformers prevail in this space, models trained on a fixed maximum length typically degrade sharply on longer inputs ( Delétang et al., 2023 ) —a failure strongly tied to positional encoding. Both sinusoidal and learned absolute embeddings ( Vaswani et al., 2017 ) , as well as unmodified rotary embeddings ( Su et al., 2024 ; Barbero et al., 2025 ) , extrapolate poorly beyond the training length. To improve extrapolation, Attention with Linear Biases (ALiBi) ( Press et al., 2022 ) replaces positional embeddings with a fixed, distance-proportional penalty on attention logits, followed by relative-position schemes like xPos ( Sun et al., 2023 ) and FIRE ( Li et al., 2024 ) , or randomized positional encodings ( Ruoss et al., 2023 ) . Remarkably, controlled comparisons on algorithmic and reasoning tasks show that decoder-only Transformers without explicit positional encodings can out-generalize ALiBi, rotary, and T5-style relative biases ( Kazemnejad et al., 2023 ) . For already-pretrained models, context windows can be extended by rescaling rotary frequencies, as in Position Interpolation ( Chen et al., 2023 ) and YaRN ( Peng et al., 2024 ) , whereas StreamingLLM ( Xiao et al., 2024 ) stabilizes infinite-stream generation via attention sinks and a sliding window (albeit discarding past context). Theoretically, length generalization has been characterized through formal frameworks with provable conditions ( Huang et al., 2025 ) , linked to whether a task admits a short program in a restricted language ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) , and attributed in part to softmax attention losing sharpness as token count grows ( Veličković et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 虽然变形器在这一空间中占上风,但经过固定最大长度培训的模型通常会因较长的投入而急剧下降(Delétang等,2023年)——这种失败与定位编码密切相关。 所学的sinusoidal和所学的绝对嵌入法(Vaswani等,2017年),以及未经修改的旋转嵌入法(Su等,2024年;Barbero等,2025年),推算都远远超出了训练时间. 为了改进外推法,注意与线性双子系统(ALiBi)(Press等,2022年)取代了位置嵌入法,在注意力对数上用固定的,相距比例的处罚来取代位置嵌入法,然后是相对位置方案,如xPos(Sun等,2023年)和FIRE(Li等,2024年),或随机定位编码(Ruoss等,2023年). 值得注意的是,对算法和推理任务的可控比较显示,没有明确定位编码的解码器唯一的变形器可以将ALIBI,回旋,和T5风格的相对偏差(Kazemnejad等,2023年)排出一般. 对于已经经过训练的模型,上下文窗口可以通过缩放回旋频率来扩展,如"位置国际化"(Chen等,2023年)和"YARN"(Peng等,2024年)中,而"流出LLM"(Xiao等,2024年)则通过注意力汇和滑出窗口(尽管抛弃了过去的上下文)来稳定无限流出. 理论上,长度通俗化的特征是通过具有可证明条件的正式框架(Huang等,2025年),与任务是否接受受限制语言的短程序相挂钩(Zhou等,2024年),部分归因于软马克思的注意力会随着物证计数的增长而失去锐度(Veličković等,2024年).

blocks.en: Beyond these extrapolation limits, standard Transformers are also bottlenecked by quadratic 𝒪 ⁡ ( N 2 ) \mathcal{O}(N^{2}) compute and linear 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ) \mathcal{O}(N) KV-cache memory growth. Yet replacing full attention with sub-quadratic alternatives exposes a fundamental tension in sequence modeling: compressing arbitrarily long histories into a fixed-size recurrent state creates an information bottleneck that degrades exact in-context retrieval, associative recall (such as key-value lookup), and zero-shot length extrapolation. Recent analyses ( Fichtl et al., 2026 ) argue that these structural deficiencies in precise memory routing prevent linear-complexity models from matching the algorithmic fidelity of full attention. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) ( Scarselli et al., 2009 ; Kipf and Welling, 2017 ; Gilmer et al., 2017 ) , which propagate information across structured relational topologies via iterative neighborhood aggregation, offer a compelling alternative and have recently demonstrated strong length extrapolation on key-value retrieval tasks ( Fink, 2026 ) . However, while GNNs have been applied in natural language processing to encode syntactic dependency trees or word-document co-occurrence graphs ( Yao et al., 2019 ; Wu et al., 2023 ) , and to augment pretrained language models with corpus-level retrieval graphs ( Meng et al., 2022 ) , their potential as a standalone, syntax-free causal backbone for sequence modeling remains largely unexplored.

blocks.en: To resolve these limitations without sacrificing efficiency, this paper introduces LimeTree ( li near- me mory graph- tree ), a purely linear-complexity architecture that reconciles language modeling quality with exact associative recall. Expanding upon the graph-tree formulation Fink (2026) , LimeTree adapts the topology with novel architectural features tailored for autoregressive token-sequence modeling. Specifically, LimeTree reformulates sequence modeling as a graph problem by constructing a hierarchical tree directly over the input tokens and applying GNN message passing across the resulting edges. Rather than trading retrieval fidelity for sub-quadratic scaling, the training regime integrates key-value lookup objectives directly alongside language modeling, enabling efficient long-range routing and exact associative recall within a strictly linear compute and memory footprint. Empirical evaluations show that LimeTree scales reliably across multi-GPU configurations to large corpora, achieving a competitive token-level perplexity of 19.76 19.76 on WikiText-103 and 10.86 10.86 (corresponding to a word-level perplexity of 37.49 37.49 ) on the long-context PG-19 benchmark, while maintaining 100 % 100\% accuracy on synthetic key-value retrieval tasks. Crucially, the architecture exhibits exceptional zero-shot length extrapolation: it preserves 100 % 100\% retrieval accuracy on sequences 32 × 32\times to 128 × 128\times longer than its training context, and when trained on sequences of at most 4,096 4,096 tokens, maintains a stable perplexity below 12 12 ( 11.38 11.38 ) out to 524,288 524,288 tokens—the hardware memory limit of a single Nvidia Quadro RTX 6000 Pro BSE GPU—thereby overcoming the primary bottlenecks that have historically restricted standalone sub-quadratic models.

blocks.en: 2 Methods
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: First, we introduce the two benchmark datasets Wikitext 103 and PG19 as well as the setup for the added key-value pair task. This is followed by the construction of the graph-tree over the token sequence and the architecture of the GNN, which is slightly different for models on the two datasets. The model on Wikitext is somewhat simpler, reflecting the smaller size and higher perplexity scores that are possible to achieve. The model for PG19 has some added features. At the end of this section we outline how the setup is adapted to work on multiple GPUs.
blocks.zh: 首先,我们引入了两个基准数据集Wikitext 103和PG19,以及添加键值对任务的设置. 随后在符号序列和GNN架构上构建出图树,对于两个数据集上的模型来说,图树略有不同. 维基文库上的模式略为简单一些,反映了可以实现的尺寸较小和难度更高的分数. PG19的型号有一些附加的特征. 在本节末尾,我们概述了如何调整设置,使之适用于多个GPU的工作.

blocks.en: 2.1 Datasets and Evaluation
blocks.zh: 2.1 数据集和评价

blocks.en: Word-to-Token: Text is converted into tokens, each of which is a short word or a subword fragment. We use the GPT2TokenizerFast implementation from the Hugging Face transformers library Wolf and et al. (2020) , which is backed by the Rust-based tokenizers library Moi and Patry (2023) . The tokenizer applies byte-level Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) with a vocabulary of 50,257 tokens. Because the input is first mapped to bytes, any Unicode string can be encoded without out-of-vocabulary tokens; a leading space is encoded as part of the following token and is displayed as the special character Ġ . The fast implementation produces the same tokenization as the pure-Python GPT-2 tokenizer while being substantially faster on large batches, and it additionally provides offset mappings that link each token to its character span in the original string.

blocks.en: WikiText-103 Merity et al. (2018) : WikiText-103 is a word-level language modeling benchmark released by Salesforce Research. It comprises over 103 million training tokens drawn from 28,475 “Good” and “Featured” Wikipedia articles, with a vocabulary of roughly 267,000 word types (all words occurring at least three times in the training set; remaining words are mapped to <unk> ). The original casing, punctuation, and numbers are preserved. Because the corpus consists of full-length articles rather than shuffled sentences, it is well suited to evaluating a model’s ability to exploit long-range context.
blocks.zh: 维基文库-103 Merity等人(2018年): WikiText-103是销售力研究公司发布的一款单词级语言建模基准. 它包含从28 475篇“好”和“好”维基百科文章中抽取的1.03亿多个培训符号,词汇约有267 000个字型(所有字型在培训集中至少发生3次;其余字型被绘制为 " unk " )。 原外壳,通点和数字保存. 因为这本书由全长的文章组成,而不是被打乱的句子,因此非常适合评价模型利用长距离背景的能力。

blocks.en: PG-19 rae2019compressivetransformerslongrangesequence : PG-19 is a long-form language modeling benchmark introduced by researchers at DeepMind, consisting of books from Project Gutenberg published before 1919. It contains 28,752 books, split into train (1,973,136,207 tokens), validation (3,007,061 tokens), and test (6,966,499 tokens) sets. The average book is about 69k words long, so individual documents span tens to hundreds of thousands of tokens, making the dataset a natural testbed for long-range dependencies. Its relatively small test set makes evaluation inexpensive. PG-19 is widely used to assess long-context perplexity in context-extension methods such as Position Interpolation Chen et al. (2023) , YaRN Peng et al. (2024) , LongLoRA Chen et al. (2024) , and StreamingLLM Xiao et al. (2024) . In the typical protocol, a pretrained model has its context window extended and perplexity is then measured as a function of context length on the test set or a subset of its books.

blocks.en: Key-value (KV) retrieval task data: In-context associative recall—recovering the most recent value bound to a queried key across long sequences—is a foundational capability for language modeling that typically breaks down in sub-quadratic architectures due to fixed-state memory bottlenecks ( Olsson et al., 2022 ; Fu et al., 2023 ; Arora and others, 2024 ; Fink, 2026 ) . To jointly enforce and evaluate exact long-range memory routing alongside natural language modeling, training and evaluation batches are augmented with a synthetic, unaligned KV retrieval task drawn from a disjoint symbol vocabulary offset beyond the 50,257 50{,}257 GPT-2 tokens ( 200 200 background filler tokens, 3 3 distinct keys { k 0 , k 1 , k 2 } \{k_{0},k_{1},k_{2}\} , and 4 4 discrete values { v 0 , … , v 3 } \{v_{0},\dots,v_{3}\} ). Each sequence of length N N is initialized with uniform random filler tokens and seeded with max ⁡ ( 2 , ⌊ N / 16 ⌋ ) \max(2,\lfloor N/16\rfloor) unassociated distractor values at even positions to prevent bag-of-words shortcuts. The context is partitioned into six equal contiguous segments organized into two sequential waves of three segments each; within each wave, a random permutation of the three keys is assigned freshly sampled values at odd-aligned token pairs ( 2 ​ m + 1 , 2 ​ m + 2 ) (2m+1,2m+2) . This odd alignment deliberately forces every key–value binding to straddle the binary tree’s even–odd leaf merge boundaries, testing cross-branch information routing rather than local pooling. Because the second wave overwrites all three keys from the first wave, the model must perform both cross-boundary token binding and temporal state tracking across the full context before autoregressively predicting the final values of ( k 0 , k 1 , k 2 ) (k_{0},k_{1},k_{2}) , evaluated via joint Exact-3 sequence accuracy.

blocks.en: Standard tree-structured networks suffer from gradient vanishing or norm explosion over logarithmic depths ( ∼ 12 \sim 12 levels at L = 4096 L=4096 ) and struggle when downstream queries require top-down global context to disambiguate local subtree representations. blocks.en: We evaluate our architecture across two complementary benchmarks designed to test medium-range language modeling and long-range multi-scale context extrapolation: WikiText-103 and PG-19 . In both regimes, the model is trained jointly on autoregressive language modeling (LM) and a synthetic associative Key-Value (KV) retrieval task to encourage robust long-horizon memory routing alongside local token prediction.
blocks.zh: 我们通过两个互补的基准来评价我们的架构,这些基准旨在测试中程语言模型和长程多尺度上下文推算:WikiText-103和PG-19. 在两种制度中,该模型都联合接受了关于自递性语言建模(LM)和合成关联键-Value(KV)回取任务的培训,以鼓励与地标预测同时进行强力长视距内存回路.

blocks.en: For the WikiText-103 benchmark, the language modeling objective is trained at a fixed context length of L LM = 512 L_{\text{LM}}=512 tokens. To supervise associative recall across varying memory horizons up to the full context window, the co-trained KV retrieval task samples sequences across four dyadic context lengths: L KV WT103 ∈ { 64,128,256,512 } . L_{\text{KV}}^{\text{WT103}}\in\{64,128,256,512\}. Training is conducted in a data-parallel configuration across 4 × 4\times NVIDIA Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs ( 48 ​ GB 48\text{ GB} GDDR6 VRAM per device; 192 ​ GB 192\text{ GB} aggregate cluster memory).

blocks.en: To scale the model to book-length narratives on PG-19 without incurring the prohibitive cost of training exclusively at the maximum sequence length throughout the entire optimization trajectory, we employ a stochastic multi-scale sequence-length curriculum. At each language modeling step (or epochal allocation), the training sequence length is drawn from the weighted multiset: L L ​ M P ​ G ​ 19 = [ 1024 , 2048 , 2048 , 4096 , 4096 , 4096 ] . L_{LM}^{PG19}=[1024,2048,2048,4096,4096,4096]. This sampling schedule induces a categorical distribution over context windows with probabilities: P ⁡ ( L LM = 1024 ) = 1 6 ​ ( 16.7 % ) , P ⁡ ( L LM = 2048 ) = 2 6 ​ ( 33.3 % ) , P ⁡ ( L LM = 4096 ) = 3 6 ​ ( 50.0 % ) , P(L_{\text{LM}}=1024)=\frac{1}{6}\;(16.7\%),\quad P(L_{\text{LM}}=2048)=\frac{2}{6}\;(33.3\%),\quad P(L_{\text{LM}}=4096)=\frac{3}{6}\;(50.0\%), yielding an expected training context length of 𝔼 ⁡ [ L LM ] = 2,901.3 \mathbb{E}[L_{\text{LM}}]=2{,}901.3 tokens. Half of all language modeling updates occur at the full 4,096 4{,}096 -token horizon, while the remaining updates at 1,024 1{,}024 and 2,048 2{,}048 tokens regularize intermediate positional representations and accelerate gradient throughput. Concurrently, the auxiliary KV retrieval task is expanded across seven dyadic scales spanning two orders of magnitude: L K ​ V P ​ G ​ 19 = { 64,128,256,512 , 1024 , 2048 , 4096 } . blocks.en: To evaluate language modeling performance, a 381 ​ M 381\text{M} -parameter model ( 316 ​ M 316\text{M} non-embedding) was trained on the 103 ​ M 103\text{M} -token WikiText-103 dataset with a maximum context length of 512 512 . Evaluated at this training horizon, the model achieves a test perplexity (PPL) of 19.46 19.46 . More notably, it generalizes zero-shot well beyond its 512 512 -token training window (Figure 4 (a)). With the exact same checkpoint weights, the model also carries this extrapolation over to key-value retrieval, maintaining 100 % 100\% exact-match accuracy from 64 64 up to 65,536 65{,}536 tokens (Figure 4 (b)). Even when compressing sequences orders of magnitude longer than those seen during training, the hierarchical memory slots continue to preserve specific associations.

blocks.en: Because LimeTree compresses long histories through a hierarchical tree rather than full pairwise attention, both its compute and memory demands scale linearly with sequence length. In practice, this fundamentally changes how inference behaves as prompts get longer. As shown in Figure 5 (a), whereas standard Transformers hit a quadratic bottleneck that causes processing speed to fall off at long horizons, LimeTree’s throughput climbs steadily across log-spaced context lengths—rising from roughly 65 ​ k ​ tokens/s 65\text{k}\,\text{tokens/s} at 512 512 tokens and 100 ​ k ​ tokens/s 100\text{k}\,\text{tokens/s} at 1,024 1{,}024 , up to nearly 400 ​ k ​ tokens/s 400\text{k}\,\text{tokens/s} at 65,536 65{,}536 tokens. At shorter lengths, runtime is bounded by the fixed-size causal decoder tail and kernel overhead; as the input grows, the lightweight 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ) \mathcal{O}(N) tree encoder amortizes that constant cost and keeps the GPU saturated, ingesting a full 32 ​ k 32\text{k} -token context in just over 100 ​ ms 100\,\text{ms} . Figure 5 (b) shows the corresponding memory behavior: peak VRAM consumption grows linearly with context length rather than quadratically. Because older context is folded into fixed-capacity tree slots while the causal decoder operates over a constant 256 256 -token window, the memory footprint increases at a predictable, bounded rate per token out to 32,768 32{,}768 tokens, avoiding the memory-capacity walls that limit standard self-attention.

blocks.en: To examine whether smaller, more efficient variants suffice, three LimeTree configurations ranging from 173 ​ M 173\text{M} to 381 ​ M 381\text{M} parameters were evaluated across context lengths. Up to the 512 512 -token training horizon, all three models perform comparably, reaching closely clustered test perplexities between 19.78 19.78 and 20.40 20.40 . Once pushed beyond the training window, however, their behavior diverges sharply (Figure 6 (a)). Whereas the 381 ​ M 381\text{M} -parameter model extrapolates smoothly to long horizons, the smallest 173 ​ M 173\text{M} variant degrades rapidly, effectively collapsing once the context length is quadrupled. Sufficient parameter capacity is therefore essential for learning generalizable hierarchical tree representations, even when short-context performance appears saturated.

blocks.en: Placing these results into the broader context of word-level language modeling on WikiText-103 highlights how far linear-complexity architectures have progressed (Table 3 ). Early linear models such as Gated CNNs ( 37.20 37.20 PPL) and QRNNs ( 33.00 33.00 PPL) were fast to train but struggled to capture long-range dependencies, leaving a wide gap behind quadratic Transformers like Adaptive Input ( 18.70 18.70 ), Transformer-XL ( 18.30 18.30 ), and Compressive Transformer ( 17.10 17.10 ). More recently, state-space and linear attention models have narrowed this divide, with S4 reaching 20.95 20.95 PPL, Hedgehog achieving 20.80 20.80 , and H3 and Mamba pushing down to 18.50 18.50 and 17.90 17.90 . Despite being trained with a short 512 512 -token context window, the LimeTree family—reaching 20.40 20.40 PPL at 135 ​ M 135\text{M} parameters, 19.85 19.85 at 174 ​ M 174\text{M} , and 19.78 19.78 at 381 ​ M 381\text{M} —outperforms both S4 and Hedgehog while approaching the perplexity regime of models trained on four to sixteen times longer contexts.

blocks.en: Equally striking in Table 3 is the fraction of compute required to reach this performance, alongside the clear headroom for further gains. Competitive quadratic and sub-quadratic Transformers routinely required between 500 500 and 1,920 1{,}920 V100 GPU-hours (such as 32 32 V100s for 60 60 hours in Transformer-XL or 16 16 V100s for 84 84 hours in the Routing Transformer), while modern state-space baselines like S4, H3, and Mamba relied on 8 8 datacenter A100 GPUs for 18 18 to 36 36 hours ( 144 ​ – ​ 288 144\text{--}288 A100 GPU-hours). By contrast, the LimeTree models were trained on just 4 4 previous-generation Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs in 8.5 8.5 to 15.6 15.6 hours—a total budget of only 34 34 to 62 62 GPU-hours, well noted that the Quadro RTX 8000 is somewhat slower than the A100/H100. Furthermore, whereas every baseline below 19.0 19.0 PPL in Table 3 was trained with context lengths between 1,024 1{,}024 and 8,192 8{,}192 tokens, LimeTree was constrained to a 512 512 -token training horizon with a 256 256 -token causal tail. Scaling the training window to 2,048 ​ – ​ 4,096 2{,}048\text{--}4{,}096 tokens and pairing the architecture with adaptive input embeddings provides a direct path to matching top attention baselines at a fraction of their training and inference cost.

blocks.en: The second model with a slightly more complex architecture was trained on the dataset PG19 in 35.5h on a single Nvidia Quadro RTX 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. LimeTree achieved a token-level perplexity score of 10.84, and a corresponding word-level perplexity score of 37.36 when evaluated on the test set on the training context length of L=512. Most remarkably LimeTree is able to hold a low perplexity score when evaluated over context lengths up to 512k, where it still has a PPL score of 11.38. Testing beyond the context length of 512k resulted in an out-of-memory exception on a single GPU. Table 4 shows the detailed scores over all context lengths, together the the success rate in the key-value (KV) retrieval task. LimeTree also holds up very well in the KV task, with near perfect accuracies up to 128k, while demonstrating linear memory increase (last two columns of Table 4 ). blocks.en: A detailed literature search for related benchmarking results was undertaken and Table 5 was compiled at the best effort. Benchmarking results in the literature are often difficult to compare, since evaluation techniques differ. Models throughout the literature were naturally trained on different computational setups, making also a training time comparison challenging. However, as Table 5 demonstrates, LimeTree scores very well for a minimally optimized model, with a token-level perplexity score of 10.84, which is right in the range of other models evaluated on a token-level. The word-level perplexity score of 37.36 is slightly higher than the baseline of the Transformer-XL, but given the early days of LimeTree, it already shows great potential. Most significantly, LimeTree reached these scores with markedly fewer computational resources during training; although the setups are not directly comparable, even a rough comparison indicates a substantial difference.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en: This work introduces LimeTree as a scalable alternative to standard Transformer architectures, competing directly against a diverse range of modern sequence-modeling variants. Across baseline comparisons, LimeTree immediately achieves solid mid-table benchmark performance—an encouraging foundation for a novel design that has not yet undergone the years of heavy hyperparameter and hardware optimization afforded to standard Transformers. Crucially, LimeTree exhibits characteristics that make it exceptionally compelling for next-generation Large Language Models (LLMs). Its memory footprint and computational cost scale strictly linearly with sequence length, breaking the quadratic attention bottleneck to enable lightweight yet high-capacity foundation models. This efficiency is paired with remarkable zero-shot length extrapolation: despite training on sequences of at most 4,096 4,096 tokens, LimeTree suffers negligible degradation at 524,288 524,288 tokens ( 128 × 128\times extrapolation), maintaining a competitive perplexity of 11.38 11.38 compared to 10.84 10.84 at the training horizon. By combining linear complexity with stable long-range reasoning, LimeTree offers a viable path toward LLMs capable of processing massive contexts without prohibitive training or inference costs.
blocks.zh: 这项工作介绍 LimeTree)作为标准变形器架构的可伸缩替代,直接与多种现代序列模型变体相竞争. 在基线比较中,LimeTree立即实现了坚实的中表基准性能——这是新的设计的一个令人鼓舞的基础,这种设计尚未经过多年向标准变形器提供的重超参数和硬件优化。 关键的是,LimeTree表现出了它对于下一代大语言模型(LLMs)特别有吸引力的特征. 它的内存足迹和计算成本尺度严格按照序列长度线性进行,打破了四分法的注意力瓶颈来使轻而高能的基础模型成为可能. 这种效率与显著的零射出长度外推法相配:尽管对序列进行了最多4,096,4,096个令牌的培训,但LimeTree的降解可忽略不计,为524,288,524,288个令牌(128×128分时外推法),保持了11.38 11.38的竞争性迷惑性,而培训场面为10.84 10.84分. LimeTree将线性复杂性与稳定的长程推理结合起来,为LLMS提供了一条可行的道路,能够处理大量的情况,而无需高昂的培训或推论费用。
